title: Finite-to-closure coefficient naturality of the projective-line exchange
statement:
theorem closure_exchange_naturality
    (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : PadicAlgCl.FiniteIntermediateField l)
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP k p] (hpl : p ≠ l)
    (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    (d : Diagram (Profinite.continuousMapRingObj.{u} E.1) Y
      (fun X ↦ spRationalTwist X l E))
    (d' : Diagram (Profinite.padicAlgClRingObj.{u} l) Y (fun X ↦ spQbarTwist X l))
    (s : ScalarCompatibility (Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl l E) Y
      (fun X ↦ spRationalTwist X l E) (fun X ↦ spQbarTwist X l)
      (closureLineMap l E) d d')
    (x : unit (coefficient l (some E)).X Y ⟶ d.Rq.R.obj
      (((DerivedCategory.singleFunctor (Modules (coefficient l (some E)).X
        (ProjectiveLine Y)) 0).obj (line l (some E) (ProjectiveLine Y))) ⟦(2 : ℤ)⟧)) :
    let a := Profinite.padicSubfieldRingObjToPadicAlgCl.{u} l E
    let x' := extendScalarChern a (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (s.units Y) s.lineP
      d.Rq d'.Rq s.q.square x ≫ (eqToIso d'.q_canonical).hom.app _
    let z := (scalarUnitPullIso (coefficient l (some E)).X Y).inv ≫
      (moduleObjectDerivedPullback (coefficient l (some E)).X
        (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map (x ≫ (eqToIso d.q_canonical).hom.app _) ≫
      secondTraceExchange l (some E) k p hpl Y ≫
      (secondDiagramPushIso _ Y _ d).inv.app _
    (moduleObjectDerivedPullback (coefficient l none).X
        (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y)).map x' ≫ secondTraceExchange l none k p hpl Y =
      (scalarUnitPullIso (coefficient l none).X Y).hom ≫
        extendScalarChern a (secondProjection Y) (s.units (ProjectiveLine Y)) s.lineW
          d.R₂ d'.R₂ s.p₂.square z ≫ (secondDiagramPushIso _ Y _ d').hom.app _

proof.text: Identify Rq and R2 in each diagram with the canonical right-derived functors using q_canonical and p2_canonical, retaining q_unit and p2_unit. The full-complex normalization of each supplied restriction square determines it uniquely by the right-derived universal property. Hence its scalar mate is the native scalar/direct-image comparison transported by these model identifications.

proof.text: The native scalar/pullback comparison is conjugate to that restriction/direct-image comparison. Its compatibility with composition follows by deriving the strictly commuting restriction/direct-image composition square and taking conjugates. Apply this to the two routes around the projective-line self-square, including its scheme-morphism equality. Transpose the exchange maps under the target p2 adjunction: their transposes are the pullback-square comparison followed by pullback of the q counit. The scalar push comparisons transpose to inverse scalar pull comparison followed by scalar extension of the same counits. The resulting cube is exactly coefficient_exchange_of_counit_at; thus the native exchanges commute with scalar extension without assuming either exchange invertible.

For the line, the finite-to-closure map is the prescribed colimit leg: its pullback compatibility follows from the rational and closure coprojection equation of the Cartesian Tate comparison. Shift this square by two with the canonical commuting-shift isomorphisms. All comparisons use the actual coefficient maps, not a choice of basis of the Tate line.

proof.text: Apply naturality of scalar/pullback comparison to x. Combine it with the coefficient/exchange rectangle and the unit and shifted-line squares. Express the finite base-changed adjunct as z by removing scalarUnitPullIso and secondDiagramPushIso from the finite exchange composite. Insert these isomorphisms back after extending coefficients, cancel their inverse pairs, and obtain the displayed equality. This uses no Chern normalization and does not invert an exchange.
